newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Newcrest sees potential at Ridgeway.
newsitem.headline: Newcrest sees potential at Ridgeway.

text.p: Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Thursday the Ridgeway prospect near its Cadia Hill gold project in New South WAles could produce more than 200,000 ounces of gold a year over a nine-year mine life.

At a briefing in Sydney, Newcrest chief executive Ian Johnson said the underground discovery had revealed good grade intersections of both gold and copper, and appeared metallurgically straight forward.
The capital cost was estimated at less than A$200 million, with an operating cost of less than A$150 per ounce of gold, including copper credits.
However, Johnson said this was optimistic. "Everything has to go right for that," he added.

Newcrest, which on Thursday announced a A$100 million write-down in the carrying value of its Telfer mine in Western Australia, has said it will spend A$24 million over the next 18 months on a detailed feasibility study of an underground mine at Ridgeway.
The prospect lies three km north-west of Cadia Hill near Orange in New South Wales.
Newcrest plans to put in a decline to the top of the deposit to allow more focussed definition drilling and bulk sampling.
Johnson said the Ridgeway prospect, which could begin full production in 2001, would add to the value of developing the large, open pit, low grade Cadia project.
The A$441 million Cadia Hill project is forecast to produce about 293,000 ounces of gold and 23,000 tonnes of copper a year for 12 years when production begins in late 1998.
Newcrest is also considering the possible development of the adjacent Cadia East prospect.
Newcrest shares were 11 cents firmer at A$3.46 at 4.05 p.m. (0605 GMT).
